sections.h2: Where is the Davidson County Register of Deeds and when does it take recordings?
sections.html:
The office is at 110 West Center Street in Lexington, NC 27292, and mail goes to P.O. Box 464, Lexington, NC 27293. The phone is 336-242-2150 and the fax is 336-238-2318. The building is open weekdays from 8am to 5pm, closed on county holidays, yet the office stops taking recordings at exactly 4:30pm under a rule dating from August 1, 2020.

Its stated mission covers real estate records, vital records and military service records, along with the notary oath. Counter visits get same-day recording and same-day return of vital records, and the office offers a public computer lab and self-serve kiosks for legal searches.

sections.h2: How do I search Davidson County land records?
sections.html:
Real estate searches are done online through the county's deeds search site, and records there are indexed from 1984 to the present. For anything earlier than 1984, the office asks you to contact staff directly.

  • When looking for a satisfaction of a mortgage, search under the document type Release.
  • Judgments are looked up through the Clerk of Courts office instead.
  • Attorneys are encouraged to use an e-record system or submit by mail.
  • Color-coded plats do not upload properly and will not be recorded.

The office also lists answers to common questions on whether an instrument must be notarized, whether you can prepare your own deed and whether you must be present to record.

sections.h2: What is the Davidson County tax certification rule for deeds?
sections.html:
Beginning March 1, 2019, the counter turns away any real property deed lacking a certificate from the Tax Administrator that no overdue tax is attached to the parcel. The county adopted the requirement by commissioner resolution on August 14, 2018, under G.S. 161-31.

An attorney-supervised closing offers a way around the certificate. The deed instead carries a printed line saying a North Carolina attorney prepared it and that any overdue tax will be sent to the collector out of the sale money. Without an attorney, you request a certificate from the Tax Department through its online form, and the county warns that a certificate can take up to two business days. A seller handling the sale without an attorney should file the request well before closing, because an unpaid earlier bill will halt the deed at the window.

sections.h2: What will the Davidson County office charge me to file documents?
sections.html:
Davidson County follows the uniform fees North Carolina sets by statute. The table shows the state schedule alongside two charges the county prints on its own page.

Recording charges that apply at the Davidson County Register of Deeds
ItemAmountWhere it comes from
Instrument in general$26.00 for 15 pages, then $4.00 a pageG.S. 161-10
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for 35 pages, then $4.00 a pageG.S. 161-10
Satisfaction or cancellationNo feeG.S. 161-10
Plat$21.00 per sheetG.S. 161-10
Certified copy$5.00 for page one, $2.00 a page afterG.S. 161-10
Assumed business name filing$26.00Davidson County Register of Deeds page
Card payments3% convenience fee or $1 minimumDavidson County Register of Deeds page

Excise tax on the deed is a separate charge. The statute sets it at one dollar for every $500 of price, or part of $500, and the seller settles it at the counter first.

sections.h2: Does recording protect a Davidson County buyer and seller?
sections.html:
Yes. G.S. 47-18 withholds protection from a deed, option or long lease until it is registered locally, and the order of registration settles who ranks first.

That is why a seller in Lexington, Thomasville, Denton or a rural township should treat recording as the final step and not an afterthought. Get the recorded book and page from your closing attorney, plus proof that the earlier deed of trust was released.

sections.h2: Who owes the property tax bill when a Davidson County house changes hands?
sections.html:
The tax collector bills whoever is the listing owner on January 1, and the county says a sale during the year does not erase the seller's liability for that bill. Closings normally split the bill by date, so read the settlement statement to see whether the buyer's portion was credited.

Sellers who want certainty can ask that the tax collector be paid directly out of closing funds. The tax collector's phone number is 336-242-2180, and the same office handles the tax certifications the Register of Deeds requires. Because a certificate and a recorded deed depend on each other, a seller who clears the tax account first usually avoids a delay at the recording counter.

sections.h2: How big is the Davidson County housing market?
sections.html:
Census estimates for mid-2025 show 180,182 residents, a rise of 6.7 percent since the spring 2020 base, living among 79,412 housing units. The county covers 553.18 square miles, and owners live in 74.4 percent of occupied homes.

  • Home value at the Census median: $219,100.
  • Rent at the median: $901 gross.
  • Monthly cost for owners with a mortgage: $1,355 at the median.
  • Households: 69,846, averaging 2.45 people.
  • Persons 65 and over: 20.8 percent.
  • Permits pulled for new building in 2025: 1,216.

Few people move in a given year, with 92.2 percent in their prior-year home. Those figures describe the whole county, not a single town.

sections.h2: What other records does the Davidson County office handle?
sections.html:
Beyond deeds, the office takes military discharges and assumed business name filings by mail at P.O. Box 464, and sellers who are heirs often need its vital records too. Marriage license applications are online, and the applicant then calls to schedule an appointment. A marriage license is valid for 60 days only.

Funeral homes with escrow accounts send certificate requests by fax, and orders are mailed within 48 hours. Others bring the request with payment and proof of their funeral home status, or mail it with a stamped return envelope. Heirs selling a parent's house usually need a death certificate for the estate file, so ordering a few early saves a second trip.

sections.h2: What should a Davidson County seller do before the deed goes in?
sections.html:
Work through a short list in order:

  • Pull the tax bill for the parcel and see whether anything is delinquent.
  • Decide whether an attorney will close the sale or you will request a tax certificate yourself.
  • Confirm the draftsman line and return address on the deed.
  • Arrange payment of the excise tax and filing fee for the same day.
  • Get the loan payoff and a recorded release of the deed of trust.

If the loan is in default, power-of-sale foreclosure is heard before the clerk of superior court, with ten days to file an upset bid after a sale report. Request a written payoff statement from the lender early.

faqs.q: What time does the Davidson County Register of Deeds stop recording?
faqs.a: Recording stops at 4:30pm sharp, even though the office stays open until 5pm Monday through Friday. The county put that rule in place on August 1, 2020.

faqs.q: Why was my Davidson County deed refused for taxes?
faqs.a: Since March 1, 2019, the office accepts a real property deed only with a Tax Administrator certificate showing no delinquent taxes, or under a closing attorney who agrees to pay any delinquent taxes from the proceeds. The certificate can take up to two business days.

faqs.q: How far back do the online Davidson County land records go?
faqs.a: Records are indexed from 1984 to the present. For earlier records, contact the Register of Deeds office at 336-242-2150.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Davidson County deed?
faqs.a: The seller does, at the counter, ahead of filing. The statute's rate is one dollar for each $500 of price or part of $500.

faqs.q: Can I record documents by mail in Davidson County?
faqs.a: Military discharges and assumed business name filings can be mailed to P.O. Box 464, Lexington, NC 27293. The assumed business name fee is $26.00, and a stamped return envelope is needed for return.
